_plan_check_history.reason: Plan is fundamentally invalid because it attempts to test the Algebraic Independence Hypothesis—which concerns algebraic independence of functions in function spaces—by using numerical approximation error of a neural network on a smooth analytic function. This conflates approximation capability with algebraic independence. The hypothesis is about whether certain functions satisfy any nontrivial polynomial relation with coefficients in a field (e.g., ℚ or ℝ), not about how well a network can approximate a function. The described experiment measures approximation capacity, not algebraic independence. Thus, even if the numerical results show bounded N_c(w), they do not support or refute the hypothesis.

Use symbolic algebra tools (e.g., sympy, Mathematica, or Lean) to verify algebraic independence via polynomial identity testing or Gröbner basis methods.

If numerical evidence is desired, design an experiment that tests whether a polynomial fit to sample points of the functions yields zero residual for all samples only when the polynomial is trivial—this would be a proxy for algebraic independence.
Avoid conflating approximation error (numerical) with algebraic relations (symbolic/combinatorial).
